title: 📘 UNIT 5: GLOBAL AND REGIONAL DEVELOPMENTS SINCE 1945
5.1 🌍 The Aftermath and Consequences of WWII
notes:
World War II caused massive human and economic losses.

Major consequences:
• About 55–62 million people died.
• Millions became homeless refugees.
• European industrial infrastructure was heavily destroyed.
• European borders were redrawn.
• Germany and Korea were divided.
• China and Eastern Europe became communist.
• Israel was created.
• Colonial independence movements accelerated.
• USA and USSR emerged as the two superpowers.
• The world became bipolar.
• The UN, World Bank, WTO and IMF emerged as major international institutions.

title: 5.1.1 🤝 Yalta and Potsdam Conferences
notes:
Yalta Conference → February 1945.

• Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin participated.

• Discussed Germany's division and the future of Eastern Europe.

• Agreed on punishment of war criminals.

Potsdam Conference → July 1945.
• Planned Germany's post-war settlement.
• Discussed Japan's surrender and occupation.

📌 These Allied conferences helped shape the post-war international order.

title: 5.1.2 ⚖️ War Crime Trials and the Holocaust
notes:
Holocaust → systematic mass murder carried out by Nazi Germany, with Jews as the largest group of victims; about 6 million Jews were killed.

Nuremberg Trial → 1946.
• Tried major Nazi leaders.
• Crimes → crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity.

Tokyo Trial → 1946–1948.
• Tried Japanese military and political leaders for similar crimes.

📌 War-crime trials established international accountability for major wartime crimes.

title: 5.2 🇺🇳 The United Nations Organization (UN)
notes:
United Nations → international organization established in 1945 after WWII.

Main aims:
• Maintain international peace and security.
• Develop friendly relations among nations.
• Promote international cooperation.
• Solve economic, social, cultural and humanitarian problems.
• Encourage peaceful settlement of disputes.

Headquarters → New York, USA.

title: 5.2.1 🏛️ Principal Organs of the UN
notes:
The six principal organs are:

• General Assembly → represents all member states.

• Security Council → responsible for international peace and security.

• ECOSOC → coordinates economic and social activities.

• Trusteeship Council → supervised trust territories and promoted independence.

• International Court of Justice → judicial organ; located in The Hague.

• Secretariat → administrative organ headed by the Secretary-General.

⚠️ Security Council → 15 members; 5 permanent members have veto power.

title: 5.3 💰 Post-War Global Socio-Economic Recovery and Developments
notes:
After WWII, the world became divided into two major economic and political spheres:

🔵 West → mainly influenced by the USA.

🔴 East → dominated by the USSR.

Western Europe received major American economic assistance.

Marshall Plan → US European Recovery Program designed to rebuild Western Europe.

COMECON → Soviet-led economic cooperation system for socialist countries.

title: 5.3.1 🇺🇸 Marshall Plan
notes:
Marshall Plan → proposed by US Secretary of State George C. Marshall in 1947 and implemented from 1948.

Aims:
• Rebuild European economies.
• Increase industrial production.
• Promote economic cooperation.
• Prevent economic and political instability.
• Reduce communist influence in Western Europe.

📌 More than $13 billion in US aid was provided.

title: 5.3.2 ☭ Molotov Plan and COMECON
notes:
Molotov Plan → Soviet economic assistance program for Eastern European socialist states.

COMECON → Council for Mutual Economic Assistance, established in 1949.

Purpose → economic cooperation and coordination among socialist countries.

📌 It functioned as the Soviet bloc's economic counterpart to Western economic cooperation.

title: 5.3.3 🌎 First World, Second World and Third World
notes:
First World → USA, Canada, Japan, Western Europe and their allies.

Second World → USSR, China, Cuba, Vietnam and their allies.

Third World → mainly countries with colonial histories in Africa, Asia and Latin America that remained outside the two major Cold War blocs.

📌 The term Third World later became associated with developing countries and the Global South.

title: 5.4 ❄️ Cold War Realities
notes:
Cold War → prolonged political, military and economic rivalry between the USA and USSR after WWII.

Usually dated from → 1947.

Characteristics:
• Arms race.
• Nuclear weapons competition.
• Military alliances.
• Propaganda.
• Espionage.
• Economic pressure and trade restrictions.
• Space race.
• Proxy wars.

Major confrontations → Berlin Blockade, Berlin Wall and Cuban Missile Crisis.

title: 5.4.1 🛡️ NATO
notes:
NATO → North Atlantic Treaty Organization.

Established → April 1949.

Original members → 12 Western countries including USA, UK, France, Canada and Italy.

Purpose → collective defense; an attack against one member was treated as an attack against all.

Headquarters → Brussels, Belgium.

title: 5.4.2 🔴 Warsaw Pact
notes:
Warsaw Pact → military alliance of communist European states dominated by the USSR.

Established → 14 May 1955.

Main members → USSR, Poland, East Germany, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria and Albania.

Cause → Western Germany's rearmament and admission to NATO.

Dissolution → 1991.

title: 5.4.3 🕊️ Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
notes:
NAM → association of countries that avoided formal alignment with either Cold War power bloc.

Bandung Conference → April 1955; important step toward NAM.

Formal establishment → September 1961, Belgrade, Yugoslavia.

Main principles:
• Independent foreign policy.
• Opposition to colonialism.
• Rejection of domination by major powers.
• Support for national independence.

title: 5.4.4 🚀 Major Cold War Developments
notes:
• Arms race → competition in nuclear and conventional weapons.
• Space race → competition in rockets, satellites and space exploration.
• 1956 → Hungarian Revolution.
• 1961 → Berlin Wall built.
• 1962 → Cuban Missile Crisis.
• 1968 → Prague Spring.
• 1970s → Détente and improved US–Soviet relations.
• 1979 → Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
• 1985 → Gorbachev became Soviet leader.
• 1986 → Chernobyl accident.
• 1989 → Berlin Wall fell.
• 1991 → Soviet Union collapsed.

title: 5.4.5 ☭ Gorbachev's Reforms
notes:
Mikhail Gorbachev → Soviet leader from 1985.

Perestroika → economic and political restructuring.

Glasnost → openness; encouraged wider public discussion and criticism.

Effects:
• Political liberalization.
• Warmer relations with the West.
• Reduced Soviet control over Eastern Europe.
• Collapse of communist governments in Eastern Europe.
• Contributed to the end of the Cold War and USSR.

title: 5.5 🌏 Situations in Asia during the Cold War
notes:
Major Asian developments included:

• Post-war Japan and rapid economic growth.
• Indian independence.
• Communist revolution in China.
• Vietnam War.
• Korean War.
• Conflicts and political changes in Indochina.

title: 5.5.1 🇯🇵 Post-War Japan
notes:
Japan surrendered → 15 August 1945.

US occupation under General Douglas MacArthur:
• Demilitarization.
• Democratization.
• Dissolution of ultranationalist organizations.
• Release of political prisoners.
• Democratic education.
• Women's suffrage.
• New constitution → effective 1947.

Economic growth factors:
• High savings.
• Education and technology.
• Skilled and relatively inexpensive labor.
• Government economic policies.
• Access to raw materials and export markets.
• US support.

title: 5.5.2 🇮🇳 Indian Independence
notes:
Indian independence movement → 1857–1947.

Indian National Congress → founded in 1885.

Mahatma Gandhi → promoted non-violence and civil disobedience.

Muslim League → represented Muslim political interests.

Quit India Movement → major anti-British campaign during WWII.

1947 → British India divided into:
• India → predominantly Hindu.
• Pakistan → Muslim-majority state.

title: 5.5.3 🇨🇳 China
notes:
Chinese Civil War → Communist forces led by Mao Zedong defeated the Nationalists.

1949 → People's Republic of China established.

Major communist measures:
• Land reform.
• Nationalization.
• Collectivization.
• Socialist economic transformation.

📌 China became a major communist power during the Cold War.

title: 5.5.4 🇻🇳 Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia
notes:
Indochina → Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia.

Vietnamese struggle:
• Anti-colonial struggle against France.
• Division of Vietnam into North and South.
• North Vietnam supported by communist powers.
• South Vietnam supported mainly by the USA and its allies.
• Vietnam War became a major Cold War conflict.

📌 Communist forces eventually defeated South Vietnam and US-supported forces.

title: 5.5.5 🇰🇷 Korean War
notes:
Korea → divided into North Korea and South Korea after WWII.

1950 → North Korea invaded South Korea.

Major sides:
• North Korea + China + Soviet support.
• South Korea + UN forces led mainly by the USA.

1953 → Armistice ended active fighting.

📌 Korea remained divided around the 38th parallel.

title: 5.6 🌍 The Middle East
notes:
After WWI → Ottoman territories were divided mainly between Britain and France.

After WWII:
• Arab nationalism increased.
• European influence declined.
• Israel was established.
• Arab-Israeli conflict became a major regional issue.
• Internal and interstate conflicts continued.

Major regional issues → Palestine, Israel, Arab nationalism, Suez Crisis and oil politics.

title: 5.6.1 🇮🇱🇵🇸 Arab-Israeli Conflict
notes:
Zionism → movement supporting a Jewish national homeland in Palestine.

Balfour Declaration → 1917 British declaration supporting a Jewish national home in Palestine.

1948 → Israel declared independence.

Arab-Israeli wars included:
• 1948 Arab-Israeli War.
• 1956 Suez Crisis.
• 1967 Six-Day War.
• 1973 Yom Kippur War.

📌 The conflict became one of the central political issues of the modern Middle East.

title: 5.6.2 🚢 Suez Crisis
notes:
1956 → Egypt nationalized the Suez Canal.

Britain, France and Israel attacked Egypt.

Outcome:
• International pressure forced the attackers to withdraw.
• Egypt retained control of the canal.
• British and French influence in the Middle East declined.
• USA and USSR became more influential in regional affairs.
• Arab nationalism strengthened.

title: 5.6.3 🛢️ Oil and OPEC
notes:
OPEC → Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries.

Major aims:
• Coordinate petroleum policies.
• Protect oil-producing countries' interests.
• Increase control over oil resources.
• Influence oil prices and revenues.

📌 Oil became an important source of political and economic power in the Middle East.

title: 5.7 ☭ Dissolution of the Communist Bloc and Its Aftermath
notes:
Factors weakening Communist rule:
• Economic problems.
• Political dissatisfaction.
• Nationalist movements.
• Gorbachev's reforms.
• Reduced Soviet control over Eastern Europe.
• Growing demands for political freedom.

1989 → Communist governments collapsed across Eastern Europe.

1991 → Soviet Union dissolved.

📌 The collapse ended the Cold War and transformed the international political system.

title: 5.7.1 🧱 Fall of the Berlin Wall
notes:
9 November 1989 → Berlin Wall opened.

Significance:
• Symbolized the collapse of communist division in Europe.
• Increased movement between East and West Germany.
• Accelerated German reunification.

October 1990 → East and West Germany reunited.

title: 5.7.2 🌐 Post-Cold War Developments
notes:
After the collapse of communism:

• USA became the dominant global superpower.
• Former communist states introduced political and economic reforms.
• Globalization accelerated.
• International trade and communication expanded.
• New regional conflicts emerged.
• Ethnic and nationalist conflicts increased in some areas.
• New security concerns included terrorism and human security.
• Information technology rapidly expanded.
